sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Colors, fonts, and shadows for the brand
sections.what: Declares the dark background, the lime green and blue accent colors, the mono and sans fonts, glow shadows, glass blur levels, and rounded corner sizes. Pages use these as ready-made class names.
sections.why: Likely reason: one place for the brand look so all pages match.
sections.watch_out: Some pages use color names that this file does not define, so those elements will not get the intended color.

summary: Defines the site's color palette, fonts, shadows, and corner rounding so that Tailwind class names can use them.
purpose: Sets the brand look in one place. Names such as goku-black, lime-robin, and blue-500 point to specific colors used across the pages.
why: Keeping colors and fonts in one file makes it easier to change the brand look later. Reason not stated in the code beyond that.
how: Tailwind reads this file at build time. It scans the page and component files for class names, then generates only the styles that are used, using the values defined here.
inputs: Class names written in page and component files.
outputs: Generated CSS classes for colors, fonts, shadows, blur, and rounded corners.
risks: Several pages use class names such as nous-cream, nous-brown, and nous-accent that are not defined here, so those parts may show no intended color. Changing a color here changes it everywhere.
debug: If a color looks wrong or plain, search the page for the class name and check that it exists in this file. Restart the dev server after edits.
